**Hyperbolic volume of representations of fundamental groups of cusped 3-manifolds**

*Stefano Francaviglia12*

38 pp, 8 sections.

**Abstract.** Let W be a compact manifold and let ρ be a representation of its fundamental group into PSL(2, C). Then the volume of ρ is deﬁned by taking any ρ-equivariant map from the universal cover f W to H3 and then by integrating the pull-back of the hyperbolic volume form on a fundamental domain. It turns out that such a volume does not depend on the choice of the equivariant map. Dunﬁeld extended this construction to the case of a non-compact (cusped) manifold M, but he did not prove the volume is well-deﬁned in all cases. We prove here that the volume of a representation is always well- deﬁned and depends only on the representation. Moreover, we show that this volume can be easily computed by straightening any ideal triangulation of M. We show that the volume of a representation is bounded from above by the relative simplicial volume of M.

**Outline.** Front matter; Introduction; General definitions; The straightening; Volume of representations; Comparison with simplicial volume; Rigidity of representations; Corollaries
